one_liner: Hosted ecommerce platform for building online stores, selling and managing orders.
auth_notes: Admin API calls send an access token in X-Shopify-Access-Token. Tokens come from OAuth authorization code grant (apps outside admin), token exchange (embedded apps, ID token -> access token), client credentials grant (only stores in the app's own organization), or client credentials with a signed client assertion (public apps, any installed store). Offline (default) and online tokens; delegate access tokens. Admin-created custom apps can no longer be created.
access_notes: Free-to-build path: dev stores (up to 250 per organization, test-only, no real transactions) created via Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI with a Partner account. Installing on arbitrary merchants requires public distribution via the Shopify App Store, which requires Shopify approval and a one-time App Store registration fee; unreviewed 'unpublished' public apps are deprecated. Custom distribution is limited to one store / one Plus org / dev stores. Protected customer data fields and some scopes need separate Shopify approval for public apps.
api_breadth_notes: GraphQL Admin API covers products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, discounts, metafields, bulk operations, etc. (hundreds of queries/mutations); cost-based rate limits. REST Admin API is legacy since 2024-10-01 and new public apps must be GraphQL-only since 2025-04-01. Storefront API also available.
mcp_notes: Shopify Dev MCP (@shopify/dev-mcp, local stdio via npx, docs/schema help, no auth). Per-store hosted endpoints: Catalog MCP at https://{shop}/api/ucp/mcp (replaced removed Storefront MCP catalog/cart tools), Customer Accounts MCP, Checkout MCP (authenticated/signed). No official hosted MCP for Admin API store management found.
blocker: Multi-merchant OAuth install requires App Store review/approval
notes: Also fetched: shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest (REST legacy), shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/dev-dashboard/development-stores (dev store limits), shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/storefront-mcp, shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks (HTTPS, Google Pub/Sub, EventBridge destinations; X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 verification). Fetched pages did not state that Partner accounts/dev stores are free (shopify.com/partners page silent on cost). Build toolkit on GraphQL Admin API; store domain ({shop}.myshopify.com) is per-tenant.

one_liner: Open-source WordPress plugin that turns a self-hosted WordPress site into an online store.
auth_notes: REST API v3 uses consumer key/secret generated in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API (per WP user, read/write/read_write). Over HTTPS: HTTP Basic auth (key as username, secret as password) or query params. Over HTTP: one-legged OAuth 1.0a signed with HMAC-SHA1/SHA256. Apps can request keys via /wc-auth/v1/authorize (keys POSTed to callback URL). MCP uses WordPress Application Passwords instead of REST keys.
access_notes: Core WooCommerce plugin is free; REST API enabled by default, merchant generates keys in admin. Requires pretty permalinks (not 'Plain'). No vendor gate, but every store is self-hosted at its own domain.
api_breadth_notes: About 30 resource groups (coupons, customers, orders, order notes, refunds, products, variations, attributes, categories, tags, reviews, reports, tax rates/classes, webhooks, settings, payment gateways, shipping zones/methods, system status, data) with CRUD + batch endpoints; well over 100 operations.
mcp_notes: WooCommerce MCP (developer preview): abilities registered via WordPress Abilities API, exposed by the separate MCP Adapter plugin at https://{store}/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server. Remote use via @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote proxy with WP username + Application Password; local via `wp mcp-adapter serve` (STDIO). Abilities: products query/create/update/delete, orders query/notes/update status. Old /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint removed in WooCommerce 11.3 (HTTP 410).
blocker: Self-hosted: per-store base URL and admin-generated keys
notes: No vendor-hosted sandbox; testing means running your own WordPress + WooCommerce install (free). Webhooks are configurable via admin UI and the /webhooks REST resource. Legacy REST API webhooks need the separate Legacy REST API plugin. Toolkit must collect store URL + consumer key/secret per connection; HTTPS strongly preferred so Basic auth can be used instead of OAuth 1.0a signing.

one_liner: SaaS ecommerce platform for B2C and B2B online stores, including headless commerce.
auth_notes: Store-level API accounts: static access_token sent as X-Auth-Token (created by merchant in Settings > Store-level API accounts). App-level API accounts: per-store token via OAuth grant code flow (single-click apps registered in Developer Portal). Account-level API accounts for GraphQL Account API. Storefront tokens (JWT, Bearer) for GraphQL Storefront API; Customer Login JWT. Legacy API accounts no longer issued.
access_notes: Any merchant store (free trial, then paid plan) can create store-level API accounts self-serve. Partner Portal sandboxes are for partners. OAuth draft apps install only on stores tied to the developer's email; installs on other stores require Marketplace approval as published or unlisted (unlisted only for approved partners who signed the partner agreement).
api_breadth_notes: REST Management API (catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkouts, content, marketing, settings, themes, inventory, locations, sites/routes, payments, B2B Edition), GraphQL Admin, GraphQL Storefront and GraphQL Account APIs; hundreds of operations.
mcp_notes: Store Management MCP (early access, admin): hosted at https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp or https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/mcp, OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, tools for products/prices, inventory, promotions, orders/refunds, store details; store owner must enable. Storefront MCP (shopper-facing, GA, per-store URL, no admin auth), WebMCP (browser), and Docs MCP at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
blocker: Multi-store OAuth app needs Marketplace approval; trial expires
notes: developer.bigcommerce.com now 301-redirects to docs.bigcommerce.com. Fetch of bigcommerce.com/free-trial failed (HTTP 403), so trial length (search snippets say 15 days) and card requirement are unverified. Sandboxes page (docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/docs/overview/sandboxes) describes creation only via Partner Portal and does not state cost. Practical toolkit path: per-store API token (X-Auth-Token + store_hash), or OAuth once the app is approved.

one_liner: Salesforce's enterprise B2C commerce platform for large-brand storefronts.
auth_notes: B2C Commerce API (SCAPI) Admin APIs: OAuth2 client credentials against Account Manager with an API client (client ID/secret, scopes chosen up front); bearer JWT in Authorization header. Shopper APIs use SLAS (Shopper Login and API Access Service) public/private clients. OCAPI is the legacy API family and needs its own client. Requests also need organization ID and short code.
access_notes: No self-serve signup or free trial on the pricing page; all tiers (Growth, Plus, Premium) are 'Contact for pricing' with on-demand sandbox credits included. API clients are created by a realm's Account Manager administrator, so credentials require being a B2C Commerce customer or working through one (e.g. as a Salesforce partner).
api_breadth_notes: SCAPI Shopper and Admin API families (products, catalogs, pricing, promotions, orders, customers, inventory, baskets/checkout, search, CDN, etc.); the official MCP docs cite nearly 600 SCAPI operations. OCAPI (legacy) also available.
mcp_notes: B2C DX MCP server (@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp) from the SalesforceCommerceCloud GitHub org: local stdio via npx; docs search, SCAPI code mode, cartridge deploy, Managed Runtime publishing, debugging, WebDAV, CIP analytics; uses your B2C config and Account Manager sign-in. Search results also mention a pilot shopper-facing B2C Commerce MCP Service via account executive (not verified by fetch).
blocker: Needs a customer realm/Account Manager; no self-serve sandbox
notes: All developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce pages returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so auth details come from search-result summaries of those pages plus the commerce-sdk README (client_credentials token via ShopperLogin) and B2C developer tooling guide. Trailhead on-demand sandbox pages opened but did not state eligibility; sandboxes are credit-based and tied to the license. Verdict is borderline blocked: building/testing requires a customer realm or partner access. Per-tenant config: org ID, short code, site ID, realm.

one_liner: Open-source (Magento) and Adobe-licensed ecommerce platform, self-hosted, PaaS or SaaS.
auth_notes: PaaS/on-prem/Open Source: admin and customer tokens (Bearer) obtained with credentials; integrations created in Admin (System > Extensions > Integrations) yield consumer key/secret + access token/secret for OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-signed) requests; session cookies for JS widgets. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS): Adobe IMS access tokens only (user or server-to-server OAuth2).
access_notes: Magento Open Source is published by Adobe on GitHub under OSL 3.0/AFL 3.0, so anyone can self-host and create integrations for free. Adobe Commerce (PaaS/SaaS) is a licensed product; credentials come from each merchant's admin or Adobe IMS.
api_breadth_notes: Web API framework supports REST, GraphQL and SOAP; PaaS REST covers catalog, inventory, sales/orders, customers, carts/checkout, CMS, store config, etc. ('wide range', no count given); SaaS REST is a smaller subset, with GraphQL for shopper flows.
mcp_notes: Adobe ships developer-tooling MCPs only: Commerce App Builder MCP server and Dropins AI Tools, installed via `aio commerce extensibility tools-setup` (appear local; for building App Builder apps/storefronts, not operating on store data). Store-data MCPs found (CData, StackOne, Marketplace extensions) are third-party.
blocker: Per-store base URL and admin-created integration; SaaS uses IMS
notes: Webhooks: Adobe Commerce Webhooks module (PaaS and Cloud Service) per developer.adobe.com/commerce/extensibility/webhooks/, plus Adobe I/O Events; not confirmed for Magento Open Source, and the older web API get-started page still says webhooks are unsupported. Base URLs differ: PaaS https://<host>/rest/<store_view>/V1/..., SaaS https://<server>.api.commerce.adobe.com/<tenant-id>/... Using integration tokens as standalone Bearer tokens may need to be enabled in store config (not verified in fetched pages). No vendor sandbox; test by self-hosting Open Source.

one_liner: Website builder with built-in ecommerce, scheduling and marketing tools.
auth_notes: API keys: generated in site Settings > Advanced > Developer API Keys, per-API permissions, shown once, no expiry; require Commerce Advanced plan. OAuth 2.0 auth code (login.squarespace.com) for Extensions: access tokens 30 min, refresh tokens 7 days and single-use (access_type=offline). Scopes: website.orders(.read), website.transactions.read, website.inventory(.read), website.products(.read), website.contacts(.read), website.discounts(.read). User-Agent header required.
access_notes: OAuth client registration is reviewed and approved by Squarespace before credentials are issued (listing in Extensions is a separate process). API keys skip review but need a Commerce Advanced plan on the merchant site. Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth-only.
api_breadth_notes: Commerce APIs: Analytics, Contacts, Discounts, Inventory, Orders, Products, Profiles (maintenance mode), Transactions, Webhook Subscriptions, plus a Websites API; roughly 30-50 operations.
mcp_notes: No Squarespace-published MCP found; only third-party servers (StackOne, Zapier, MCPBundles, community GitHub projects).
blocker: OAuth client needs Squarespace review; API keys need paid plan
notes: Each token is bound to a single website. Did not verify whether trial sites can generate API keys or whether a developer test site is offered. Base URL https://api.squarespace.com/.

one_liner: Ecwid by Lightspeed: embeddable online store builder for adding ecommerce to any site.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (external apps): install redirects to redirectUrl with code and store_id; backend POSTs to https://my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token/{store_id} with client_id/client_secret/code/redirect_uri. Returns non-expiring per-store bearer access_token (secret_...) and optional public_token (public_...). Store owners get tokens for their own custom app without OAuth. Native apps receive an encrypted payload. Scopes like read_catalog, update_orders, read_customers.
access_notes: Only stores on paid plans can access the API; developers can get a free upgrade or test store by emailing Ecwid support. Multi-store public apps start with a Request form; once approved Ecwid provides a free Premium test store and dev app, and App Market listing needs app validation review.
api_breadth_notes: REST API groups include store profile, orders (incl. abandoned carts, order calculation), products (variations, reviews), customers and customer groups, categories, discounts/coupons/promotions, plus app storage/settings; likely 100+ operations (no exact count on fetched pages). Rate limit 600 req/min per token.
mcp_notes: No Ecwid/Lightspeed-published MCP found; only third-party connectors (Zapier, viaSocket, Unified.to, Apideck).
blocker: Paid plan for API; multi-store OAuth app needs Ecwid approval
notes: Also fetched docs.ecwid.com/develop-apps/app-settings (token types, scopes, webhookUrl requirement) and docs.ecwid.com/launch-apps/steps-to-go-live-with-a-public-app (request form -> free Premium test store -> validation). Webhooks are configured per app via webhookUrl (static HTTPS). Sandbox = free test store on request. api-docs.ecwid.com redirects to docs.ecwid.com.

one_liner: Platform for creators to sell digital products, memberships and courses.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 applications created in Gumroad Settings > Advanced; the application page also yields an access token for the owner's account. Official CLI supports OAuth device authorization, browser PKCE, or a raw access token (GUMROAD_ACCESS_TOKEN). Scopes reported in search results: view_profile, edit_products, view_sales, mark_sales_as_shipped, edit_sales, view_payouts (not verified on a fetched official page).
access_notes: Any Gumroad account can create an OAuth application and access token at no cost (no plan gate found; Gumroad charges per-sale fees). No app review was mentioned in fetched sources.
api_breadth_notes: v2 API: user, products (enable/disable), variants, offer codes, custom fields, files, sales (refund, mark shipped), subscribers, licenses (verify/enable/disable), payouts, resource subscriptions (webhooks); roughly 30-40 endpoints.
mcp_notes: Gumroad MCP at gumroad.com/mcp, published by Gumroad, Inc.: remote, per-assistant connector URL, OAuth to the seller's account; read sales/products/buyer emails/payouts, draft and publish/unpublish products. Community servers also exist (rmarescu/gumroad-mcp, keithah/gumroad-mcp).
notes: gumroad.com/api and the help article gumroad.com/help/article/280-create-application-api were fetched but their bodies did not render (JS), and Mintlify mirrors returned HTTP 410; API surface is inferred from the antiwork/gumroad-cli README (third-party-ish, under the antiwork org that hosts the Gumroad source) and n8n's credential docs (third party). Webhooks = resource_subscriptions (sale, refund, etc.) plus legacy Ping. Base URL https://api.gumroad.com/v2/.

one_liner: Amazon SP-API for sellers and vendors to manage listings, orders, inventory and reports.
auth_notes: Login with Amazon (LWA): selling partner authorizes app (OAuth) -> refresh token; exchange at https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token for 1-hour access token sent in x-amz-access-token header. Grantless operations use client_credentials with scopes (sellingpartnerapi::notifications, ::client_credential:rotation, ::shipments:track). PII operations need a Restricted Data Token (RDT) from the Tokens API. Fetched example request carries no SigV4 signing.
access_notes: Register as private (own org; needs a Professional Seller Central account; individual accounts ineligible) or public developer (OAuth to other sellers; must list in Selling Partner Appstore). Developer profile includes security questionnaire; all roles require Amazon approval, restricted (PII) roles need extra data-use/security justification. A $1,400/yr third-party developer fee + usage fees were announced for 2026 but reportedly cancelled (could not open Amazon's notice; 404).
api_breadth_notes: 40+ API sections (orders, catalog items, listings items, product type definitions, FBA inventory, fulfillment inbound/outbound, reports, feeds, finances, notifications, pricing, fees, shipping, tokens, vendor APIs); several hundred operations.
mcp_notes: Local SP-API Dev MCP (sp-api-dev-mcp) in Amazon's amzn/selling-partner-api-samples GitHub repo: Developer Assistant server (API execution, catalog exploration, migration help, codegen, docs search) and Workflow server. No hosted MCP found. Many community servers exist.
blocker: Developer profile and role approval by Amazon required
notes: developer-docs.amazon.com now 301-redirects to developer-docs.amazon. Also fetched roles-in-the-selling-partner-api (5 restricted roles; all roles need approval) and the-selling-partner-api-sandbox (static + dynamic hosted sandboxes, 5 rps). Webhooks = Notifications API delivering via Amazon SQS/EventBridge, not plain HTTPS callbacks. Regional endpoints (NA/EU/FE) and marketplace IDs are per-connection config. Fee status rests on third-party search results only.

one_liner: Commas (formerly FanBasis): checkout, payments, funnels, courses and webinars for creators.
auth_notes: No public API docs found. Zapier's Commas integration states it connects via OAuth. Vendor site advertises 'APIs and SDKs' but gives no auth details.
access_notes: Enterprise & APIs page targets high-volume sellers with 'Open account' and Contact Us calls to action and a dedicated implementation engineer; no public developer portal, docs or self-serve key flow found. Pricing not published.
api_breadth_notes: No reference docs found. Zapier app exposes 18 instant triggers (new sale, refunds, failed payments, disputes, subscription events, webinar registrations, referral commission, Discord join) and no actions.
mcp_notes: commas.com homepage lists 'MCP (beta)': run Commas from an AI assistant to create checkout links, issue refunds and pull numbers. No endpoint, setup docs or hosting details found.
blocker: No public API docs; API access appears enterprise/contact-sales only
notes: FanBasis rebranded to Commas (reported July 2026; fanbasis.com now redirects/blocks). fanbasis.com and fanbasis.com/enterprises returned HTTP 403. Search snippets of the old FanBasis enterprise page claimed a REST API, Postman collection, webhooks, sandbox and Node/Python/PHP/Ruby SDKs, but these could not be opened or verified. Zapier instant triggers suggest push events exist. 'rest' in api_style is unverified. Contact Commas for API docs/credentials before scoping a toolkit.
